dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: #Oh, it's you, {NICKNAME}. How have your recent travels been?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: If there's anything you need, just tell me anytime.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: It's quite different from Aaru Village, but I feel at ease here nonetheless.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I was so surprised the first time I came in. Such a small teapot, and yet so vast on the inside...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: If I could store Aaru Village in a teapot...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: I was simply musing. Even if that were possible, what I seek to protect is not an object named Aaru Village...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: ...It is my homeland and the lives of everyone in it.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: My apologies for making you listen to all this...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: And, thank you for having me.

choices.text: That would definitely make things more convenient...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Hmm... If I could easily take everyone someplace else...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: No, I suppose they wouldn't agree to leaving the desert in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Up for a chat, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Sure, but what should we talk about...?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: If you don't mind, could you tell me about the places you've been to? Any of them will do.

choices.text: About the scenery and culture of Mondstadt...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Verdant grass, a city of song and freedom...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: I'd love to see it for myself.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: The desert has been my home my entire life. I hardly even journey to the other side of the Wall of Samiel.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: But after hearing you speak of all these faraway lands, I can't help but find the thought of traveling quite... enchanting.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You should come with us!

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Ah, it truly is a tempting offer... But I cannot forsake my duty to protect Aaru Village...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Perhaps your words will take root within my heart, and one day, my desire to see the world beyond will sprout and grow.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: When that day comes, I shall follow your footsteps.

choices.text: About the scenery and culture of Liyue...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: A nation of trade and contracts... I've heard about it before, but your description paints a whole new picture.

choices.text: About the scenery and culture of Inazuma...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: A land surrounded by the ocean, a castle built atop an island...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anything you want to do?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: If you have time, would you like to hear me tell a story?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: You can sit by my side, or... something more casual, whatever makes you feel comfortable and relaxed.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Although I may be a village guardian with her spear and shield ever at the ready... Deep down in my heart, I've always loved cozy and calm atmospheres like this.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Got it.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Great. So, just be yourself when you're around me.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Well then... weary wanderer of lands beyond, do you wish to hear about the ancient legend of King Deshret, or the history of Aaru Village?

choices.text: About the legend of King Deshret...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: King Deshret was an ancient god of the desert, known as "Ahmar" to the desert folk.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: He was the king of warriors, gardeners, and intellectuals alike. He controlled the howling winds in the desert, the sand dunes silvered by moonlight...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: And the thousand-and-one fairy folk who hid within the dreams of the night and the cries of the owl...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: His arrogant acts of folly led to his ruinous fate. The sands entombed his city, leaving only the sorrowful elegies of the Eremite songsters...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Even now, most desert folk remain devout believers in King Deshret. The rumor that he will one day be resurrected has become their only hope for the future.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: People may find it hard to admit, but lies often soothe the heart more than the truth ever could.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: My apologies... Things got dark pretty quickly.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You might feel better if you let everything out.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Heh, you're right.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: We had a difficult past, and our lives at the moment aren't exactly easy, but it's our peaceful lifestyles that I wish to defend.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Thank you for patiently listening to all that I had to say. It feels like a burden has been lifted from my heart.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: #Thank you, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: When you have time, I'll tell you more stories of the interesting things that happen in our village.

choices.text: About the history of Aaru Village...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: In the past, the mountain and lake where Aaru Village is situated was a part of King Deshret's territory.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: As the god of the desert, King Deshret built a city from the golden sand and crimson rock, and called it "Akhtamun."

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: After King Deshret passed, the surviving residents of the city became the earliest inhabitants of Aaru Village, bringing their traditions and faith with them.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Some time later, Aaru Village became a place of exile for scholars...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: We are all born free, yet we are also inevitably bound by shackles.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Candace.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Good morning. Did you rest well last night?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: The goddess of the night will be worried if you don't sleep well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Candace.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: It's getting late. Now, off to bed you go.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I hope the fathomless dark of the night will watch over your dreams and grant you a good night's sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Making a house feel like a home isn't about the physical objects. It's about creating a certain atmosphere...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Warm, intimate, safe, secure, peaceful...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Everything I seek to protect... it's all here.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I love Aaru Village's architectural style. Heh, I know I'm biased, but that's not the reason why.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Just look at these intricate patterns and beautiful facades. The ancient style really adds a lot of character, and it's all the more majestic in such a tranquil environment.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: ...Can I stay here and admire it for a little longer?
